subtitle: Machine Learning For Travel Time Forecasting
summary: A Machine Learning model combines connected vehicle data and road network information to forecast travel times on selected A90 and A91 motorway sections in the Rome area, with outputs shown in an interactive dashboard.
heroText: From traffic observations on 500 m road segments to forecasts 5, 10 and 15 minutes ahead, a dashboard connects current congestion levels with predicted travel times.

overview.title: Project at a glance
overview.text: The pilot produces travel time forecasts for selected sections of the A90 and A91 motorways in the Rome area. It combines connected vehicle observations and road network information in an interactive dashboard showing congestion levels, average speeds and forecasts 5, 10 and 15 minutes ahead.

stats.label: Motorway corridors in the Rome area

meta.Area: Rome, Italy; A90 Aurelia–Laurentina and A91 Magliana viaduct–Fiumicino Airport interchange
meta.Data: Infoblu Floating Car Data, ANAS network graph, RMT incident and roadworks data

story.label: The challenge
story.title: Anticipating changes in traffic over the next few minutes
story.text: Traffic conditions vary over time and across consecutive road segments, making travel times difficult to predict. The challenge is to turn heterogeneous datasets into consistent inputs that capture traffic patterns and support short-term forecasts.

story.label: What was analyzed
story.title: Traffic observations and road network characteristics
story.text: The analysis covers November 2022–October 2024 on selected A90 and A91 sections. It examines average speed, vehicle counts, road attributes, incidents, roadworks and weather. Coverage, anomalies and missing data inform the selection of Floating Car Data (FCD) aggregated over 500 m segments.

story.label: Our approach
story.title: From integrated observations to short-term forecasts
story.text: The approach combines transport engineering, data preparation and a comparison of six Machine Learning architectures. The selected Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) + Transformer model uses average speed and FCD vehicle count, with forecasts and performance indicators displayed in a dashboard.

data.title: Data sources

items.name: Infoblu Floating Car Data
items.text: Infoblu provides average speeds and observed vehicle counts aggregated over 500 m road segments for November 2022–October 2024.

items.name: ANAS network graph
items.text: The ANAS transport network graph provides road geometries, segment lengths, cross-section characteristics, capacity and free-flow speed.

items.name: RMT incident and roadworks data
items.text: RMT provides records of incidents and roadworks and information on their effects on traffic.

items.name: Additional sources assessed
items.text: PANAMA sensors, TMC traffic aggregations, municipal weather data and traffic orders provide additional observations and contextual information assessed during source selection.

deliverables: Travel time forecasts for 5, 10 and 15 minutes ahead support short-term traffic analysis.
An interactive dashboard combines colour-coded congestion levels, average speeds and predicted travel times.
Model performance indicators show forecast accuracy and computation times for monitoring.

methods.title: From raw data to the final product
text: Traffic observations, road network attributes and contextual records are collected and checked for coverage. Infoblu FCD are selected, cleaned and spatially linked to the network graph; missing values are filled using the latest available value for each segment. Average speed and vehicle count are standardised and scaled. Six architectures are compared across 30 configurations each, using training, validation and test splits of 70%, 20% and 10%. MAPE and RMSE guide the selection of LSTM + Transformer. The dashboard displays forecasts and performance indicators.

Temporal variables, road attributes, incident counts during the preceding hour and segment adjacency are assessed alongside traffic observations. The selected model retains average speed and FCD vehicle count. PANAMA sensors are excluded from training because of their spatial distribution and gaps in data availability.

items.text: The comparison selects LSTM + Transformer, with reported mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 17.63% and root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.45.

items.title: Final model inputs
items.text: The selected model uses average speed and FCD vehicle count over 500 m segments, following assessment of additional sources and contextual variables.

items.title: Integrated dashboard
items.text: The dashboard combines congestion levels, average speeds and travel time forecasts 5, 10 and 15 minutes ahead, alongside performance indicators.

items.title: Sensor coverage gaps
items.text: PANAMA sensor observations are excluded from training because their spatial distribution and data availability do not support the selected modelling dataset.

limits.title: Limitations and next steps
items: Results cover only the selected corridors and study period. Performance on other road sections requires further assessment.
FCD represent a sample of circulating vehicles. The source reports an RMSE of 0.45 without specifying its unit or evaluation scale.
next: Extension to a wider geographical area, assessment of model scalability.
Training of additional models for different road categories, assessment of infrastructure-specific traffic patterns.

subtitle: Julia, the virtual assistant of Rome
summary: The first urban generative AI: the virtual assistant of Roma Capitale, answering residents and visitors in real time with certified information.
heroText: The virtual assistant of Roma Capitale: documents, events, transport, culture and city services, in 80+ languages, 24/7.

julia.title: Julia, the virtual assistant of Rome
intro: Julia is the virtual assistant of Roma Capitale, presented as the first urban generative AI. Whether you are living Rome during the Jubilee, dealing with everyday life or discovering hidden corners of the city, she answers in real time with up-to-date, certified information.

She guides residents and visitors through the services of Roma Capitale and the city itself: documents and procedures, events, museums, restaurants, transport and more. A single message is all it takes to start.

items.label: Designed to evolve
items.title: Better with every release
items.text: Julia's technology improves constantly, which makes her more effective, more useful and more precise with each new release.

items.label: Certified knowledge
items.title: Every piece of data is validated first
items.text: Julia does not learn everything at once: the quality of information is verified first, and each piece of data is validated and certified before it is added. Her knowledge comes from official sources.

items.label: Multi-agent architecture
items.title: One orchestrator, many specialised agents
items.text: When a chat starts, a Super Agent orchestrator coordinates several specialised agents to produce a single, complete and reliable answer.

items.a: Julia complies with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and uses advanced encryption to protect personal information. No sensitive data is stored without explicit consent.

Julia relies on certified, up-to-date data from official Roma Capitale sources and reliable partners in tourism, mobility and culture. As with any AI, results may not be 100% certain, since they depend on the quality and completeness of the available information.
Julia uses your position only if you knowingly share it, and keeps it for a few minutes within the conversation. After that she asks you to share it again if you want location-based answers.

items.q: How does the conversation history work?
items.a: History stays active only for a limited time. Once it expires, it is as if you were talking for the first time: Julia keeps no memory of previous interactions.

items.q: How do I get the best answers?
items.a: Ask clear and precise questions, rephrase if you do not find the answer straight away, and use punctuation to separate different requests. If Julia seems stuck, write "let's start over" or "change topic".
